summary: Conservation Department 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 fire tower near Bay Shore (Brentwood), Long Island: built 1948, closed 1959, removed 1960.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower on concrete footings, with wood steps and landing platforms
facts.status_note: Removed in 1960 per the register; the land is now privately held and no source describes what remains.

access.note: The register says the land is now privately held. Ask the owner before going onto it.

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department (Bureau of Forest Fire Control)

events.note: June 8, 1945 announcement by the Long Island State Park Commission of a planned new fire tower in the vicinity of Bay Shore
Built by the Conservation Department; the Long Island page places it on a sand pit on Department of Transportation property on Fifth Avenue near Brentwood Road
Closed in 1959 when the Conservation Department curtailed forest fire control on Long Island; in October 1959 the state abandoned lookout services and the title passed to Suffolk County
Removed by the NY State Conservation Department, Bureau of Forest Fire Control
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on January 18, 2009

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Long Island page places the 1948 tower on Department of Transportation property; the register says the land is now privately held. Both can hold if the land changed hands, but no source records a sale or transfer.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on the 1948 build, 1959 closure and 1960 removal (register) and the 'Removed' status (Long Island page). The Long Island page's paragraph that says a tower was 'dismantled and removed in 1960 by a local demolition contractor' sits under the Kings Park and other tower entries, not Bay Shore, so it was not used. The 80-foot figure is the tower height from the Long Island page; no source gives a cab-floor height, so no height_m was recorded. The register calls the site Bayshore, the Long Island page Bay Shore (community Brentwood). The record's coordinates were not checked against a map. Ownership: the Long Island page says DOT property at the time; the register says privately held now. No photos found.
